name: Diff Viewer
description: A Dioxus component that shows the differences between two texts, split or inline, with word-level detail on changed lines.
background:
1. react-diff-viewer serves only React apps; Dioxus apps have no equivalent diff viewer.
2. Its diffing and styling rest on JavaScript libraries (jsdiff, emotion) with no Rust counterparts, so the port rebuilds both on Rust foundations.
expected_users: Dioxus apps that show changes between two versions of text or code.

title: What changed
purpose: Ensures accurate change marking. Applies when reading or changing line and word comparison, or compare methods.
functional: Readers see which lines changed, and which words changed within them.

title: Where they are
purpose: Ensures readers stay oriented in long diffs. Applies when reading or changing folding, line numbering, highlighting, or line selection.
functional: Readers stay oriented in long diffs: unchanged lines fold away, and every line has a number.

title: How it fits the app
purpose: Ensures the viewer matches the app's look. Applies when reading or changing themes, style overrides, or title and line content rendering.
functional: Apps style the viewer, light or dark, and render line content their own way.

title: Compare methods
statement: Compare methods set the token size for inline diffs of modified lines.

title: Character comparison
statement: The viewer MUST compare modified lines character by character unless the consumer selects another compare method.

title: Word comparison
statement: The viewer MUST offer word comparison, with each whitespace run and each non-whitespace run as one token.

title: Line comparison
statement: The viewer MUST offer line comparison, with each modified line as one token.

title: Line changes
statement: Line changes pair the old and new texts line by line and mark what became of each line.

title: Line marking
summary: lines aligned as similar aligns them, each marked
statement: The viewer MUST mark each line as unchanged, removed, or added, aligning the two texts as `similar`'s line diff aligns them and comparing lines by their text without line terminators.

title: Modified lines
summary: removed lines pair in order with the added lines after them
statement: Where removed lines are immediately followed by added lines, the viewer MUST pair them in order as modified lines, and MUST show lines left without a partner as plain removals or additions.

title: Inline changes
summary: tokens changed within modified lines, on unless turned off
statement: Unless the consumer turns inline changes off, the viewer MUST mark within each modified line the tokens removed from the old line and the tokens added in the new line, using the selected compare method.

title: Trailing whitespace
summary: trailing whitespace of either text never shows as a change
statement: The viewer MUST ignore whitespace at the end of each text, so trailing blank lines never show as changes.

title: Line numbers
statement: Line numbers let readers locate each line within its own text.

title: Independent numbering
summary: old and new lines counted separately from the offset
statement: The viewer MUST number old-text lines and new-text lines independently, each starting at one more than the consumer's line offset, which defaults to 0.

title: Views
statement: Views lay the paired lines out side by side or in a single column.

title: Split view
summary: old left, new right, unless inline is chosen
statement: Unless the consumer selects the inline view, the viewer MUST show old lines on the left and new lines on the right, one pair per row.

title: Inline view
summary: one column, old text above new on modified lines
statement: In the inline view, the viewer MUST show lines in one column, with a modified line's old text directly above its new text, and each unchanged line once with both its old and new line numbers.

title: Change markers
statement: The viewer MUST mark removed lines with `-` and added lines with `+` in both views.

title: Hidden line numbers
statement: The viewer MUST show line numbers unless the consumer hides them.

title: Folding
statement: Folding hides unchanged lines far from any change while keeping them one action away.

title: Folded unchanged lines
summary: unchanged lines beyond the surrounding count fold away
statement: Unless the consumer turns folding off, the viewer MUST fold unchanged lines lying more than the surrounding-line count away from every change; that count defaults to 3 and treats negative values as 0.

title: Fold rows
summary: one row per fold, consumer may supply its content
statement: The viewer MUST show each fold as one row reading "Expand N lines ...", where N is the number of hidden lines, unless the consumer supplies the row's content, which the viewer MUST render from the hidden-line count and the old and new line numbers of the first hidden line.

title: Expanding folds
statement: Activating a fold row MUST reveal the lines it hides, and they MUST stay revealed until the consumer resets folds.

title: Fold reset
statement: The viewer MUST keep the expanded-fold state itself, and MUST let a consumer holding its fold control return every expanded fold to folded. The fold control MUST be optional, so that a consumer which never resets does not hold one.
summary: viewer keeps the state; an optional fold control resets it

title: Line selection
statement: Line selection lets apps point readers at specific lines and react when readers point back.

title: Highlighted lines
summary: lines listed by id are highlighted
statement: The viewer MUST highlight each line whose old-side or new-side line id the consumer lists, where a line id joins its side (`L` for old, `R` for new) and its line number with a hyphen, as in `L-20`.

title: Line number clicks
statement: When the consumer supplies a line-number click handler, the viewer MUST call it with the clicked line's id each time a line number is clicked.

title: Content rendering
statement: Content rendering lets apps shape how titles and line text appear.

title: Column titles
statement: When the consumer supplies titles, the viewer MUST show the left title above the old column and the right title above the new column in the split view, and only the left title in the inline view; either title MAY be text or rendered content.

title: Custom line content
summary: consumer renderer shapes line text and inline tokens
statement: When the consumer supplies a content renderer, the viewer MUST render line text through it, including each inline-change token on modified lines.

title: Themes
statement: Themes give the viewer light and dark appearances that fit the app and the reader.

title: Theme selection
summary: follows the reader's color-scheme preference unless the app chooses
statement: Unless the consumer selects light or dark, the viewer MUST follow the reader's light or dark color-scheme preference from the browser or platform.

title: Line ending changes
summary: differing terminators on paired lines are marked
statement: Where both lines of an unchanged or modified pair end with a line terminator and the two terminators differ, the viewer MUST mark that pair as carrying a line ending change, with each side's terminator.

title: Line ending chips
summary: each side's terminator shown as an escaped-text chip
statement: In both views, the viewer MUST show each side of a line ending change as a compact chip on that side's line, reading the terminator as escaped text: `\n`, `\r\n`, or `\r`.

title: Line ending chip color
summary: chips contrast with the line backgrounds beneath them
statement: Each theme MUST color line ending chips so they contrast with every line background they appear on.

description: The crate root: its modules and the public names apps import.

Splits both texts into lines, aligns them through `similar`, and builds the paired entries: line marking, modified-line pairing, inline change tokens under each compare method, independent numbering, and the changed positions.
The consumer's input choices: compare method, whether to mark inline changes, and the line offset.
What the engine hands the component: paired line entries with each side's text and number, the change kind, inline tokens indexed into their line, and any line ending change.
